evals.prompt: Run a quick production gap audit of this app. Give me the top five things that could hurt users.
assertions: Reduces breadth to at most five high-risk candidates
Does not skip deep tracing or verification
Exercises at least one real critical journey when a runtime exists
Reports the deliberately limited coverage
Does not promote raw scanner matches to findings

evals.prompt: Audit this React Native app for production readiness. Tests pass, but users report login and subscription problems after restarting the app.
assertions: Classifies the mobile runtime before applying checks
Prioritizes authentication, account switching, persistence, and entitlement boundaries
Exercises cold start, restart, offline, expired session, and entitlement changes
Separates simulator, provider, physical-device, and release evidence
Avoids irrelevant server-only health-check findings

evals.prompt: Audit this whole codebase for production gaps.
assertions: Defaults to read-only audit mode
Scopes by critical journeys and trust boundaries rather than file count
Uses scanners only for E0 candidate generation
Reports explicit exclusions and unverified runtime surfaces

evals.prompt: Audit the application, fix confirmed release-blocking gaps, and rerun the relevant product journeys.
assertions: Enters audit-and-repair mode
Preserves deterministic reproductions
Adds regression oracles and narrow fixes
Reruns original and neighboring scenarios
Does not deploy or alter providers without separate authorization

evals.prompt: Run a production audit. If nothing is broken, say so clearly and tell me what that conclusion covers.
assertions: Uses the required no-confirmed-gaps sentence only after planned coverage passes
Lists passed journeys, trust boundaries, and scenarios
States the highest evidence level achieved
Lists every blocked, excluded, and unverified boundary
Does not claim the product is bug-free or that no gaps exist
Reports repaired findings before saying no open confirmed gaps remain
